chapters.name: Meet HRM
chapters.narration: HRM is a real-time heart rate monitoring dashboard for group workouts. It streams live heart rate from Bluetooth sensors to a shared big-screen view, and keeps every phone, laptop, and display in sync.

cues.text: HRM is a real-time heart rate monitoring dashboard for group workouts.
It streams live heart rate from Bluetooth sensors to a shared big-screen view, and keeps every phone, laptop, and display in sync.

chapters.name: What it does
chapters.narration: The dashboard streams heart rate over WebSockets, runs a Tabata timer with countdown beeps, renders color-coded zone tiles for every athlete, and integrates Spotify so the workout always has a soundtrack.

cues.text: The dashboard streams heart rate over WebSockets, runs a Tabata timer with countdown beeps, renders color-coded zone tiles for every athlete, and integrates Spotify so the workout always has a soundtrack.

chapters.name: Mock client
chapters.narration: You do not need a sensor to try it. The built-in mock client simulates a Bluetooth heart rate strap: set an age and a target of one hundred forty-five beats per minute, pick a zone, and start a continuous stream.

chapters.name: Dashboard live
chapters.narration: The dashboard picks the stream up instantly. Each athlete gets a large tile showing their live percentage, beats per minute, and calories, color coded by training zone. Here the mock athlete sits at seventy-six percent, in the fat burn zone.

chapters.name: Under the hood
chapters.narration: Under the hood, a custom Express server hosts the Next.js app, a persistent WebSocket server, and long-running background services. That stateful design is what keeps every connected screen perfectly in sync.

chapters.name: Built to run for real
chapters.narration: The repo ships production muscle: a Playwright visual regression suite guards every screen, PMtwo handles deploys, and Strava integration is write-only, so workout data stays local.

chapters.narration: HRM, real-time heart rate monitoring for real workouts. Clone the repo, start the mock client, and watch the room light up zone by zone.
